method: Borda primary (21 - rank), mean score secondary, first-place count tiebreak, seeded coin toss last

justifications.P01: The one clock every verb spends and every hunter reads; the priority queue is the engine; one more leg generalised to a thirty-year life.
justifications.P02: The scheduler is the game: time on a printed schedule is the one resource every system spends, departures leave without you, hunters ride the same Bradshaw, and all nineteen other candidates attach to its queue as event types; the cheapest to build and a proven, honest loop.
justifications.P03: The printed timetable was the period's most pervasive real constraint on a spy, and this makes it the turn, the map, the clock and the engine's one scheduler at once: travel, time pressure and directive 5 become a single object into which every other verb and every other candidate plugs; proven, honest pull (one more leg) and the most buildable spine.
justifications.P04: The frame every other candidate presupposes: a real timetable as the clock, departures as turns, owned and stale route knowledge, one event queue with exact replay; travel becomes the verb that costs time, money and traces.
justifications.P05: The scheduler made into the turn: departures as decision points, slack as the resource, routes as owned dated knowledge; the cleanest expression of directives 3 (travel) and 4 (time), and one-more-leg generalised to every verb.
justifications.P06: The temporal skeleton and the engine's heart: every verb is a timed action in the slack between departures, on a known graph bought from dated guides; honest one-more-leg compulsion.
justifications.P07: The clock every verb sits in; the independently moving world of directive 4 is native and the event queue is directive 5's heart; it needs a motive engine arranged around it.
justifications.P08: The clock everything hangs on: every verb a timed action on a real timetable, hunters on the same board; the engine spine and the 80 Days pull in one.
justifications.P09: The scheduler is the game: every verb competes for slack between real departures, the hunt reads the same timetable, and the night-train session end is the pool's most honest "one more leg" — the skeleton every other candidate already assumes.
justifications.P10: The clock the life runs on: one discrete-event scheduler, departures as decisions, routes as owned knowledge; the most feasible spine and the honest one-more-leg session structure.

justifications.P01: The Reilly career frame: paymasters' belief models reconciled on the alliance calendar give the loop its purpose, its politics and its ending.
justifications.P02: The Ace-of-Spies career as a system: several paymasters' belief stores reconciled on the alliance calendar, with the budget loop that makes your successes fund your hunters; the broadest directive coverage and the panel's widest convergence.
justifications.P03: The touchstone career as a system: several paymasters with belief stores reconciled only on the real alliance calendar (1904, 1907, 1914, 1917), with the hunt born from your own inconsistencies and a budget loop that makes your successes pay for your pursuers; broadest panel convergence and a coherent whole game.
justifications.P04: The career frame with the panel's widest support: several paymasters, reconciliation only at liaison, budgets that fund your future hunters; politics and deception as one loop, travel only secondary.
justifications.P05: The touchstone career as a system: per-paymaster belief stores, lies as consistency debt, reckonings on the alliance calendar and a hunt born from your own inconsistencies; it arranges C12, C17, C04, C20, C03 and C05 without absorbing them.
justifications.P06: The espionage half of the career as a complete game: belief stores reconciled on dated liaison events, the hunt emerging from the player's own inconsistencies, and a budget loop that makes the information economy real.
justifications.P07: The touchstone career as one system: patrons with belief stores, reports as product, reckonings on the alliance calendar, patron turned hunter; every directive hangs from it and seven panelists converged on it.
justifications.P08: The career spine: the hunt generated from your own inconsistencies on a real alliance calendar, and your deliveries fund the hunters who will read you.
justifications.P09: The touchstone career as a system: reports composed against several belief stores, lies booked as consistency debt, reckonings on the alliance calendar, your successes funding your hunters; dread and relief are caused by your own lies.
justifications.P10: The career as sustained deceit with dated reckonings and a budget loop that pays for your own hunters; the broadest panel support; the life only secondary.

justifications.P01: Legends as the unit of account, with linkage as the hunt's only advance: granular failure and the life as a portfolio.
justifications.P02: Legends as the unit of account keys every store per name and makes the hunt a linkage problem decidable on the timetable; the life sim's structural choice, with an honest endowment-effect hook.
justifications.P03: The spy's private life as the unit of account: legends that run unattended, name-bound credit, circles that gossip, and a hunt that advances only by linking names on the real timetable; the Meldewesen-versus-Britain asymmetry makes where you can invent a person a mechanic, exactly as the period had it.
justifications.P04: Legends as the unit of account for ledgers, dossiers and standing, with the timetable-incompatibility test as the canonical link; the touchstone's several lives as a system with real travel coupling.
justifications.P05: Identity as the unit of account: one dossier per name, the timetable alibi as canonical link, gossip bridges as a social linkage source; the life-sim half of the information economy, feasible and historically exact about where people are invented and where they die.
justifications.P06: Legends as the unit of account: each owns accounts, debts, burn and standing that sizes credit, and the hunt advances only by linking names; the many-household life made mechanical.
justifications.P07: The life as a portfolio of legends, with linkage the hunt's only progress: directives 2 and 4 in one entity model, and failure stays granular.
justifications.P08: Identity is the join key of every system and the hunt is linkage: derivable, auditable, granular (lose a name, not the game); the Reilly life as a data model.
justifications.P09: Legends as the unit of account make the life sim and the hunt one object: endowment on what you built, granular failure (lose a name, not the game), the timetable alibi as the canonical link.
justifications.P10: The unit of account every other candidate presupposes: names own money, paper, standing, households and dossiers, and the hunt advances only by linking two; the touchstone career made a system.

justifications.P01: Never observed, only recorded: the one evidence substrate that binds the life sim to the hunt; an append-only log that is save, replay and dossier at once.
justifications.P02: The record store every hunt candidate reads: one tuple with authorship, dossiers as views, manufactured evidence as a verb; the invariant that makes capture fair and replay exact, though thin as a standalone game.
justifications.P03: Never observed, only recorded is the archival truth of the age made into the hunt's substrate: registers, cable copies and passport desks with real coverage and lag, one tuple for records and lies, dossiers as filtered views; every hunt system reads it, so it is a spine in the engine's sense, though the player still needs a career to run on it.
justifications.P04: The one record store every hunt candidate reads; the invariant that makes capture auditable; as a spine it is a substrate with few verbs of its own.
justifications.P05: The substrate every other candidate reads: one tuple type for records and claims, dossiers as views, authorship making fabrication a verb; the engine's spine and the hunt's fairness guarantee, though more the ground than the game.
justifications.P06: The substrate every hunt candidate reads; as a spine it guarantees fairness and the one-record engine, but says less about what the spy does all day than about how it is recorded.
justifications.P07: The record substrate every hunt candidate reads; an indispensable invariant, but infrastructure rather than a defining concept.
justifications.P08: The invariant that makes every hunt candidate fair (one log, one tuple); indispensable substrate, not a thing you play.
justifications.P09: The hunt's data spine: never observed, only recorded; every deduction derivable from one log makes forty hours of pursuit auditable and manufactured evidence a first-class verb.
justifications.P10: The record substrate every hunt candidate reads; never observed, only recorded is a true period fact made into the fairness invariant; thin on economy and politics as a game by itself.

justifications.P01: The two-speed race is the pool's most legible dread, but as a spine it narrows the life toward flight and arbitrage.
justifications.P02: The engine's second graph made vivid: body at train speed, news at cable speed; one propagation layer drives the hunt, stale news and the bourse; weaker on the life, so a spine for the pressure half of the brief.
justifications.P03: The era's unique physics as a game: a body on the timetable against a description on the wire, with agency territories, office hours and the 1914 cable cuts as real latencies, and bourses that reprice only when news lands; honest dread made legible, bounded now by self-forecast and trade records as evidence.
justifications.P04: Two graphs, two speeds: body by train, description and news by wire; hunt, markets and the player's window on the world all fall out of latency, with the self-forecast keeping it fair.
justifications.P05: Body at train speed against news at cable speed is a crisp, legible dread, and the self-forecast fix keeps it honest; the market attachment and the pure-flight risk make it a hunt spine rather than a life spine.
justifications.P06: Two graphs, one race: legible dread and the only market model that scales, bounded emergently by depth, evidence and prescience; as a spine it risks collapsing into flight.
justifications.P07: Body at train speed, name at wire speed: a unifying race that also carries news, markets and censorship; a whole game, though hunt-heavy.
justifications.P08: The period's defining asymmetry (wire against train) as the shared mechanic of hunt and market; dread legible, the self-forecast honest.
justifications.P09: Body at train speed, description at cable speed: a complete, legible race that fuses travel, hunt, coding and markets; near-misses are earned, not rolled.
justifications.P10: Body at train speed against news at cable speed is a superb race, but after amendment its substrate is C17 and the life is absent; risks pure flight.

justifications.P01: The campaign frame: exits, succession and skills grown by use honour directive 2, but it shapes the ending rather than the turn.
justifications.P02: The campaign frame: one persistent world, failure costs the agent not the player, exits as declarative queries, skills that rust; an event-sourced life record with snapshots keeps replay exact.
justifications.P03: The frame of a life: three clocks, use-grown and rusting skills, steerable exits and a persistent world in which losing the agent never loses the campaign; the right container for thirty years, but a frame rather than a loop.
justifications.P04: The campaign arc: ageing, rust, steerable exits and a persistent world across agents; an honest one-more-job structure, light on travel.
justifications.P05: The life frame: three clocks, steerable exits, skills that grow by use and rust, a world that outlives the agent; it gives the campaign a finite shape and makes failure cost the agent, not the player.
justifications.P06: The life frame that gives money its terminal meaning: an estate valued at the day's exchange, steerable exits, ageing and rust, and failure that costs the agent rather than the campaign.
justifications.P07: The campaign frame: ageing, skill rust, steerable exits and one world across agents; the only candidate carrying RPG progression and an honest ending structure.
justifications.P08: The campaign frame: ageing, exits, succession; failure costs the agent, not the player; thin as a daily loop.
justifications.P09: The campaign frame: a life designed to end, exits as steerable states, succession in a world that remembers; failure costs the agent, never the player's competence, so retention survives loss.
justifications.P10: The only candidate that makes the spy a life across decades: three clocks, ageing and rust, exits as steerable states, succession without losing the world; the frame C04 lives inside.

justifications.P01: The hunter as a legible mind on the same timetable, now playable from both chairs; directive 4's fairness proof, though it presupposes C07 and C17.
justifications.P02: Scotland Yard on a real timetable: hypotheses propagated on the transport graph and reweighted only by delivered records, cordons only where men can be in time, and an inverse mode that teaches the engine by use; cheap with bitsets.
justifications.P03: Scotland Yard made geographic and fair: hunters who ride the same Bradshaw, reason only from delivered records and cordon only where their men can be, now playable from both chairs; the finest antagonist engine in the pool, but the antagonist is not the spine of a life.
justifications.P04: The hunter as a mind on the same Bradshaw: noisy reachability, cordons only where men can be in time, and the inverse mode that teaches the engine by use; Scotland Yard made geographic and legible.
justifications.P05: Scotland Yard from both chairs on a real Bradshaw: hypotheses that cannot teleport, cordons only where men can be in time, and an inverse mode that makes the hunter legible by use; the strongest honest fairness argument for forty hours of pursuit.
justifications.P06: Hunters that reason and ride the same timetable, now playable from both chairs; the fairest hunt in the pool, though a pursuit is a phase of a life, not its spine.
justifications.P07: The Scotland Yard touchstone made geographic, fair and now two-seated, with superb feasibility; a hunt engine rather than a life.
justifications.P08: The hunter as a mind on your timetable, now two-seated; the fairest hunt in the pool, but an antagonist system rather than a whole life.
justifications.P09: Hunters bound by the same Bradshaw and budgets, reasoning only from delivered records; the inverse mode teaches the belief engine by operating it — the fairest antagonist in the pool.
justifications.P10: The Scotland Yard directive realised fairly, with the inverse mode that gives C11's turning exit a system; the antagonist's engine rather than the game.

justifications.P01: The world model and parameter layer that directives 1 and 5 need; ventures add a verb, yet the player's loop still lives elsewhere.
justifications.P02: The accuracy contract as data: Tier 0 rails, Tier 1 windows, pressure with saturation, one dated parameter layer and a computed inquest; essential to directive 1, less compulsive minute to minute.
justifications.P03: The constitution that lets accuracy and agency coexist: immovable Tier 0 dates, jittered Tier 1 holders and contracts, free Tier 2, one dated parameter layer every regime table reads, priced foreknowledge and ventures scored on extraction; indispensable as the world's rule set, thinner as the player's minute-to-minute loop.
justifications.P04: Directive 1 as an engine: Tier 0 rails, saturating pressure, one dated parameter layer and a computed inquest, now with ventures as a verb; the world's chassis more than the player's.
justifications.P05: Tiers make directive 1 mechanical and the inquest gives systemic closure; ventures at last give it a player verb, yet it remains the history layer the others stand on rather than the career itself.
justifications.P06: Directive 1 as a mechanic and the engine's single parameter layer; ventures and prescience give it verbs, but day-to-day play is reading the field rather than acting in it.
justifications.P07: Solves the owner's paradox (history accurate, the player's scale perturbable), is now the parameter layer every candidate reads, and ventures plus the inquest give it verbs and closure.
justifications.P08: How to be accurate and still matter; the parameter layer and ventures give it verbs, but it defines the world more than the player's loop.
justifications.P09: The world-model contract: immovable rails, bounded switchpoints, a computed inquest, ventures scored on extraction; protects directive 1 but plays thin minute to minute.
justifications.P10: Directive 1 and the parameter layer made mechanical, with ventures as the counter-revolution pillar; the world's clock, but thin player verbs and no life.

justifications.P01: The goal generator: world-state wants and windows, exclusive by travel time and paid on corroboration; honest scarcity with no quest log.
justifications.P02: The content engine of directive 5: factions post wants with windows from world state, offers exclude one another by travel time, payment on corroboration; needs a wide template library and planners, so moderate cost.
justifications.P03: The content engine: factions derive wants from world state and post located, time-windowed jobs made mutually exclusive by travel time and paid on corroboration; it supplies motive without authored missions, with the standing risk of samey templates.
justifications.P04: The content engine the prohibition demands: factions post located, time-windowed jobs that exclude each other by travel time and pay on corroboration; a generator rather than a spine.
justifications.P05: The content engine: wants and windows from faction planners, mutually exclusive by geometry, now bounded by pay-on-corroboration; essential for unauthored content, thinner as a defining fantasy.
justifications.P06: The demand side: factions that plan, pay on corroboration and hire rivals; no authored missions, mutual exclusivity by geometry; abstract alone, indispensable beside C15.
justifications.P07: Faction agency generating the board from world state is the content engine politics needs; the risk of samey jobs keeps it below the career spines.
justifications.P08: Infinite coherent content without authors; a generator more than an experience, and sameness is the risk.
justifications.P09: The content engine: factions post located, time-windowed jobs that exclude each other by geometry; honest scarcity and counterfactual feedback, though sameness is its retention risk.
justifications.P10: The procedural job board is the right content engine beneath a spine; as the spine it turns the life into a quest log.

justifications.P01: A complete career spine in which two loops relieve each other's pressure; narrower than C01 and prone to the tycoon spreadsheet.
justifications.P02: Commerce as the engine of espionage with two books and concession projects: strong directive-2 coverage and history, but polity stability and rival bidding are heavier AI and travel and the hunt go secondary.
justifications.P03: Commerce as the engine of espionage, with the firm's two books as the artifact that hangs you and concessions as projects with real preconditions (irade, guaranteeing bank, legation) converging to history; a coherent tycoon-spy game whose hunt is thinner than the identity-based spines.
justifications.P04: Business that funds spying and spying that wins business, with the firm's books as the hanging artifact; a strong career shell with slow pacing between deals.
justifications.P05: Business funds spying and spying wins business, with the books as the hanging artifact; coherent and period-true, but here the information economy is instrumental rather than central.
justifications.P06: The only hook that makes commerce and espionage one loop, as the touchstone career does; it pays for every other system and gives travel, politics, deception and the hunt (the books, the receiver) their reasons.
justifications.P07: Business funds spying and spying wins business while the books hang you; a coherent career spine whose pacing between deals is slow.
justifications.P08: The best answer to what you do all day: commerce as the engine of espionage; the hunt only secondary.
justifications.P09: The commerce half of the touchstone career as a spine: business funds spying, spying wins business, the books hang you; strong interlocking loops, a slower hook, spreadsheet risk.
justifications.P10: The commerce half of the touchstone and the visible means of support every legend needs; long payoffs interleaved with short tension; spreadsheet risk.

justifications.P01: The thirty-second decision: one cost vector of money, time, health, standing and trace that every system prices from the same field.
justifications.P02: The atomic decision of the whole game: every purchase carries money, time, health, standing and trace, harvested at four disclosure points; fundamental to fairness, too thin to be the game alone.
justifications.P03: The thirty-second decision of the age, sleeper against register with the body paying for silence, is historically exact and gives every night consequence; as the defining concept it is a pricing layer, not a game.
justifications.P04: The thirty-second decision the whole game is made of, class against register with the body keeping the books; indispensable as a layer on C07, thinner as a standalone spine.
justifications.P05: The thirty-second decision with a body attached: a clean approach-avoidance loop and the register as the price of comfort; a dial every day, not a spine.
justifications.P06: The cleanest daily dilemma (sleeper or register) with the body keeping the books; a cost vector every system reads, not a career to arrange them around.
justifications.P07: The thirty-second dial between comfort and cover, now with a body that keeps books; honest approach-avoidance, but a dial is not a spine.
justifications.P08: The thirty-second decision the hunt hangs on, with the body now attached; a texture layer rather than an organising principle.
justifications.P09: The pool's cleanest thirty-second decision, with the body paying for silence; attributable consequence every night, but a dial needs a career to turn it.
justifications.P10: The thirty-second decision the game is made of, now carrying the body, convalescence and ageing; honest approach-avoidance tension, narrower on economy and politics.

justifications.P01: The motive: burn and debt as a second clock and creditors as a second hunter make the player go out and be seen.
justifications.P02: Instruments, dated debts and obligations as the forcing function that ends turtling, with creditors as budgeted hunters; excellent period mechanics, infrastructure rather than the frame.
justifications.P03: Money with a body and debt with a calendar, obligations to people as leverage lines, creditors as the second hunter and the 1914 to 1923 regime arc as scheduled catastrophe; the forcing function that stops turtling, essential beneath a spine rather than the spine.
justifications.P04: Instruments with weight and names, debts on a calendar, creditors and dependants as a second hunter; the forcing function that stops turtling, secondary on travel.
justifications.P05: Money with weight, debt with a calendar, obligations as leverage lines and creditors as the second hunter; the forcing function against turtling, strong on time pressure, narrower on deception.
justifications.P06: The cost side closed against exploits: instruments with a name, debts with a calendar, obligations as leverage, creditors as hunters; a spine would still need C15's income to make the loop whole.
justifications.P07: Instruments, dated debts and obligations as leverage lines, with creditors as the second hunter; the economy's spine, but a ledger rather than a game.
justifications.P08: Burn rate and creditors as the second hunter stop turtling; a forcing function, not a spine.
justifications.P09: Money with a body and debt with a calendar stop turtling and make creditors a second hunter; a forcing function rather than a frame.
justifications.P10: The life's money and obligations as the second hunter, now with dependants and the borrow-then-burn bound; a pillar that needs C04's names to attach to.

justifications.P01: Jurisdiction, liaison and the archive are period mechanics of the first rank; a layer of the hunt, not its spine.
justifications.P02: Jurisdiction, liaison and archives as history made mechanical, now with offence framing; a superb layer over the hunt, not a spine.
justifications.P03: Jurisdiction as terrain, now correctly built on the 1870 Act's political-offence exception and the 1886 treaty, with capitulations, dated liaison channels and archives that reopen; the hunt's true political geography, but it frames the pursuit rather than generating the career.
justifications.P04: Jurisdiction as terrain with the 1886 treaty corrected and archives that never close; a politically rich hunt layer that needs C05 and C17 beneath it.
justifications.P05: Who may know what, when: jurisdiction, offence framing, liaison edges and archives that reopen; a superb constraint layer on the hunt that needs a career to constrain.
justifications.P06: Jurisdiction, offence framing and the undeleted archive as terrain; the past catching up by mechanism, strongest as the hunt's political geography rather than as the whole game.
justifications.P07: Alliances as the hunt map and archives that never forget make the hunt a political process; a layer on C17 and C10, not a spine alone.
justifications.P08: The hunt's political geography and long fuse; superb macro-structure with no daily loop of its own.
justifications.P09: Jurisdiction and liaison as terrain with archives that never forget; historically the richest constraint map, but a map rather than a loop.
justifications.P10: The decades-long hunt and jurisdiction as terrain: sanctuary, exile and the archive that reopens; the long-arc dread a thirty-year life needs.

justifications.P01: The only conversation system in the twenty and a fine one; a subsystem every candidate needs, not a spine.
justifications.P02: Conversation as typed claims with maturities, the only systemic conversation model in the pool; a necessary interaction layer with costly NPC agenda AI that cannot carry travel or the hunt alone.
justifications.P03: Conversation as a game of claims, evidence and calls with lies as maturing debts fills the one directive sub-area the pool otherwise left to ledgers, and interrogation leaks the dossier; necessary and sound, but a scene mechanic rather than a spine.
justifications.P04: The only conversation game in the pool and a necessary organ, with lies as dated debts; as the game's spine it would subordinate the network to the room.
justifications.P05: The only conversation system in the pool and the tactical half of every lie is a debt; indispensable to directive 3, but as the whole game's spine it would organise the social layer alone.
justifications.P06: Conversation as claims and calls, lies as debts, bribery against a hidden price: the best social system in the pool, which needs another candidate to supply the journey and the money.
justifications.P07: Conversation as claims, calls and lie-debts is the deception directive's engine; an excellent system that is narrow as a spine.
justifications.P08: Conversation as claims and calls is the pool's only real talk system; indispensable, yet not what the game is about.
justifications.P09: Conversation as claims, calls and maturing lies is the only honest probe into what others believe; an essential verb, a narrow spine.
justifications.P10: Conversation as claims and calls, with lies maturing as debts, is the best scene-level system in the pool; essential, but a scene, not a life.

justifications.P01: War as a regime over a yearly disruption layer is the best vertical slice of the engine, not the defining concept.
justifications.P02: Crisis ladders, the disruption layer and war as a regime overlay with Tier 0 fixed; the best vertical slice in the pool, but episodic set-pieces rather than the thirty-year spine.
justifications.P03: Crisis ladders with literal deadlines, mobilisation overwriting the civilian graph, a yearly disruption layer and the war read by counting carriages make warfare a process the player travels through; episodic by nature, so a superb regime layer rather than a thirty-year spine.
justifications.P04: Mobilisation seizing the player's trains, the yearly disruption layer and a wartime network that is different rather than closed; a superb regime, episodic as a thirty-year spine.
justifications.P05: The richest period process in the pool and the 1914 hinge every candidate needs; as a spine it is a regime overlay and a vertical slice, not the thirty-year career.
justifications.P06: Crisis ladders, mobilisation and the war regime are historically superb overlays and the ideal vertical slice, but a regime is something the spine passes through, not the spine.
justifications.P07: Crises, mobilisation and war as the macro time pressure, with the tier rule explicit; the strongest warfare candidate, but episodic across thirty years.
justifications.P08: War as regime and disruption layer: a vertical slice of the world clock, not the spine.
justifications.P09: Crisis ladders and the war regime give pure, unstoppable countdown tension; as a spine it is a four-year slice of a thirty-year brief.
justifications.P10: War as a yearly disruption layer and a regime you prepare for is strong directive-1 and directive-4 material, but as spine it makes 1895 to 1913 a prologue.

justifications.P01: Papers and provenance are the items directive done right; they consume the record store rather than define the game.
justifications.P02: Documents as composed items with inspector depth and provenance as a C17 view; the items directive done right and a knowable frontier test, but a subsystem of travel and deception.
justifications.P03: Documents as composed, provenanced items tested against dated regimes and inspector depth, with the 1914, 1915 and 1920 flips as mechanics; the best items layer in the pool, and a layer is what it is.
justifications.P04: Papers as composed items and the frontier as a shaped-odds test, the dated requirement table included; an essential items system, not the clock.
justifications.P05: Documents as composed, regulated, provenanced items with inspection depth; the best items subsystem in the pool and the supply side of every paper regime, but a subsystem.
justifications.P06: Items with provenance and inspection as a shaped-odds test on one record store; the artifact model the economy needs, but too narrow a daily loop to be the spine.
justifications.P07: Documents as composed, provenanced objects facing a knowable test; the best items system, secondary by nature.
justifications.P08: Excellent item and inspection model; a subsystem of frontiers and forgery.
justifications.P09: Composed documents, depth-profiled inspectors and provenance make every frontier a knowable test; a complete item system, not the game's organising principle.
justifications.P10: Items and inspection as a knowable test are a true pillar of directive 3, but a subsystem rather than a spine.

justifications.P01: Itineraries for everything is sound logistics with a project-management risk; a subsystem of C07.
justifications.P02: Generalises the scheduler to everything that moves and compiles plans into it; one planner for all agents is a real saving, but logistics is the operational layer, not the defining concept.
justifications.P03: Luggage, crates, couriers and plans as itinerary holders on one scheduler is logistically true to the period and gives a second cliffhanger, but as the defining concept it tends toward the spreadsheet the sources themselves warn of.
justifications.P04: One planner for everything that moves: luggage, crates, couriers and sub-agents compile into the scheduler; a strong travel and items spine with a spreadsheet risk the bounding only partly removes.
justifications.P05: Itineraries for everything and plans compiled into the scheduler; a genuine logistics game with honest hooks after amendment, yet a body-first spy life risks becoming a dispatcher's board.
justifications.P06: The spy as network operator with cargo on the freight timetable and visible customs odds; a coherent game whose spreadsheet risk is real and whose hunt is borrowed.
justifications.P07: Everything with an itinerary gives logistics depth and real cliffhangers, but risks decentring the body.
justifications.P08: One planner for all agents is elegant, but a logistics spine risks project management over a life.
justifications.P09: Itineraries for crates, couriers and plans add a second cliffhanger and honest delegation loops; as a spine it drifts toward project management.
justifications.P10: Logistics with two bodies in play is deep and feasible but drifts toward project management and leaves the person out.

justifications.P01: Habit mining is a sharp hunt layer whose meaning depends on C04, C05 and C17.
justifications.P02: Habit mining and the obligation calendar on one scheduler; a strong dilemma, but a layer that consumes C17 and feeds C05.
justifications.P03: Habits as evidence, obligation calendars and itinerary plausibility turn upkeep into stealth and feed the hunters' inference; a fine inference layer that presupposes every other system.
justifications.P04: Habits, itinerary templates and alibi profiles mined by the hunter; the plausibility-versus-predictability dilemma is real but is a layer on C04 and C05.
justifications.P05: Plausibility against predictability is a dilemma that never resolves and habit mining is a fine hunter input; as a defining concept it is one inference pass over C17.
justifications.P06: Plausibility against predictability turns upkeep into stealth, a genuine insight; as a spine it is a hunter inference layer over lives defined elsewhere.
justifications.P07: Plausibility against predictability is a dilemma that never resolves; a valuable layer on C04 and C05.
justifications.P08: The plausibility-versus-predictability dilemma is real; as a spine it is one inference layer consumed by C05.
justifications.P09: Plausibility against predictability never resolves, so upkeep becomes stealth; a superb binding layer that presupposes legends and hunters rather than organising them.
justifications.P10: Plausibility against predictability turns upkeep into stealth; the dilemma that makes the life sim itself tense; presupposes C04, C05 and C17.

justifications.P01: The player's windows onto the hunt are essential feedback design, but feedback is not a spine.
justifications.P02: The feedback layer: windows on inference, the press as mirror, interrogation, and the deterministic autopsy that doubles as the engine's debugger; indispensable for fairness, not a game by itself.
justifications.P03: The windows into hunter inference and the replayable autopsy are the fairness contract the whole hunt depends on, but a contract about what the player may see cannot be the concept the player plays.
justifications.P04: The hunt's interface and autopsy, now cleanly separated from own-trail views; indispensable presentation, not a concept to build the game around.
justifications.P05: The right answer to how the player reads hunter inference, and the autopsy is the fairness device; but it is a presentation layer with no spine of its own.
justifications.P06: Essential fairness and interface layer (windows, autopsy) that makes the hunt trustworthy; it presents the game rather than being it.
justifications.P07: The epistemic rule that keeps the hunt fair; essential design law, least spine-like.
justifications.P08: The fairness interface for forty hours of pursuit; essential, but by definition a window onto other systems.
justifications.P09: The fairness contract of the hunt: windows and autopsy convert loss into mastery; indispensable to any spine, but not one itself.
justifications.P10: An interface philosophy for the hunt that every build needs, not a concept to build the game around.

justifications.P01: The coding ladder is necessary to directive 3 and well bounded; a subsystem, never the spine.
justifications.P02: A well-built coding subsystem with templated ciphertexts and an abstraction ladder; it fills the thinnest directive sub-area but cannot organise the other systems.
justifications.P03: Cable copies, learning censors and hand-breakable ciphers make coding a stealth system rather than a puzzle and are historically precise; vital as directive 3's coding pillar, impossible as the spine of a life.
justifications.P04: Coding made a real skill with a paid rung and the source-burning dilemma; the sub-area the slot was reserved for, but a subsystem by nature.
justifications.P05: Coding as a real system with a ladder, half-lives and the burn-the-source wager; necessary for directive 3 and assumed by five other candidates, but no game should hang from its ciphers alone.
justifications.P06: A superb coding subsystem with an honest mastery ladder and the source-burning wager; too narrow a verb set to carry a thirty-year life.
justifications.P07: Coding done properly, with an abstraction ladder and learning censors; a required subsystem, not a spine.
justifications.P08: Fills the coding sub-area with a real mastery ladder; the narrowest coverage of the twenty.
justifications.P09: The abstraction ladder is honest competence design and the coding directive's only primary home; too narrow to arrange travel, economy and politics around.
justifications.P10: Coding is a named directive and the ladder is honest, but a puzzle layer cannot be the spine of a life.

P01.statement: Build the clock first. C07 makes the timetable the turn: every verb in the game — meet, cable, forge, trade, bribe, register — is an action with a duration placed in the slack between departures, so travel, deception, items, economy and politics all spend the one resource the hunters also read. That is what turns six deep systems into one game rather than six minigames. It is directive 5 made literal: one priority queue of timestamped events is the engine, the save (seed plus input log) and the world that moves without you. It realises Bradshaw's and 80 Days as mechanics — routes as owned, dated knowledge, the connection as the atomic unit of tension — and its compulsion is the honest kind: one more leg, generalised to a thirty-year life. Everything else in the twenty (C17's records, C02's prices, C01's masters, C18's jobs) hangs from this spine without modification.

P02.statement: C07 is the spine because it is the one scarce resource every other system spends: time on a printed schedule. Travel (directive 3) is its skeleton; time pressure (directive 4) is native, since departures leave without you and the hunters read the same Bradshaw; deception, items, economy and politics are actions with durations competing for the slack between connections; the life is a diary of rent days. It is historically exact as mechanics: the monthly Guide, the transfer at the gauge break, bank hours, ice closures, a network that changes by date. Its compulsion is the proven, honest kind: the near-missed connection, the booked departure not yet earned, sessions that end aboard a night train. For directive 5 it is literally the engine: a global priority queue with total ordering, so a save is seed plus input log and every consequence is a scheduled event. All nineteen other candidates attach to it; none runs without it.

P03.statement: The period's most pervasive constraint on a spy was the schedule: trains, steamers, mails, bank hours and registration deadlines ran on printed timetables, and C07 makes that schedule the game's turn structure. Every verb (a meeting, a cable, a forgery, a drawing at a bank) spends time in the slack between departures, so travel (directive 3), time pressure (directive 4) and the engine's single scheduler (directive 5) are one object, and the spy's life (directive 2) becomes a diary read against Bradshaw's. Accuracy is mechanics, not decoration: monthly editions go stale, the Russian gauge break forces a change of train, 1914 deletes services, tunnels and airlines shrink the world across thirty years. Every other candidate plugs into its slots: hunters on the same graph, reconciliations on alliance dates, quarter-days, mobilisation overwriting the civilian timetable. Its pull is proven and honest: one more leg, sessions ending aboard a night train.

P04.statement: C07 is the one candidate that is a frame rather than a feature. It makes the world a timetable: every verb the other nineteen propose, a forged paper, a bribe, a bill falling due, takes hours and must fit between departures that leave whether or not you are ready. That satisfies Directive 3's Bradshaw's and 80 Days touchstones literally (real connections, fares, classes, owned and stale route knowledge on a date-versioned, multi-modal network), Directive 4 structurally (the world advances through the same queue; hunters ride and read the same timetable) and Directive 5 cheaply (one priority queue, exact replay from seed plus input log, connection-scan routing). Its addiction is honest: the connection just made, the booked departure not yet earned, the night train that ends a session mid-journey. Arrange C13's second graph, C05's hunters, C04's legends and C18's jobs around it and you have one game, not six.

P05.statement: C01 is the touchstone career made mechanical: several paymasters each hold a model of you, and every lie you tell is a debt that a dated reconciliation can call in. As a spine it arranges the other systems without absorbing them: C12 is how claims are made, C17 is what records exist, C04 is which name they attach to, C20 is the cipher each service reads, C03 and C10 are the alliance calendar that schedules the reckonings, C05 and C16 are what happens when a belief flips to double. Its hook is honest: dramatic irony, near-misses you controlled, each added master a self-set difficulty slider; and its engine is bounded by design, since stores are compared only at liaison. It invents nothing: 1904, 1907, 1914 and 1917 are the reckonings, and the budget loop means your successes fund the hunters who will one day read you.

P06.statement: C15 is the only candidate whose hook is the touchstone's own career: commerce and espionage as one loop, the private life paid from the same books. It answers directive 2 literally — spy career, business career and personal life as one resource system, hunted through its own records — and gives every other system its reason. Travel, because grants sit in Constantinople, Tehran, Peking. Deception, because the firm is a legend with paper. Items, because deeds, tenders and ledgers are artifacts. Politics, because grants are won through legations and voided in 1908, 1914, 1917. Time pressure, because decrees, options and bills mature. The hunt, because the books hang you and bankruptcy hands them to a receiver. Its compulsion is honest tycoon psychology — long payoffs, near-solvency, sell or hold — under a life-and-death hunt on sunk costs. Project objects with political preconditions are a direct, feasible test of the engine.

P07.statement: C01 is the touchstone career as a system: several services and principals pay you at once, each holding a belief store about you, and your product is the report, composed from held tokens and fabrications and scored for novelty and corroboration. Every directive hangs from that loop. Politics is the patron and the calendar of reckonings (1907, 1914, 1917) at which stores are compared; deception is the report and the consistency debt paid by making lies true; economy is retainers and a budget loop in which your credited successes fund the hunters who will read you; travel is handlers in several capitals; the hunt is the patron who flips; time pressure is a liaison date you can see coming. It needs C10 as its world and C17 as its record, and arranges both. Its hook is honest — dramatic irony, near-misses you controlled, betrayal born of your own inconsistencies — and seven of ten panelists converged on it independently.

P08.statement: The Legend Portfolio is the spine because identity is the join key of this entire game. Every other candidate is already written per name: C08's ledger, C17's records, C05's dossiers, C06's papers, C07's circuits, standing per circle. Build the legend as the unit of account and the other nineteen attach without seams. It is directive 2 verbatim — several identities, households in several cities, the past catching up — and it is Scotland Yard transposed from location to identity: hunters never see you, only names, and advance only by linking two, with the timetable-incompatibility test making that link decidable and auditable. Failure is granular — lose a name, not the game — which is what lets forty hours of pursuit stay fair. The history is mechanical, not decorative: Britain is where names are invented until 1915, Germany where they die. Engine cost is bounded: unworn identities run at low detail.

P09.statement: Build the timetable first. C07 makes the world a discrete-event simulation whose only decision points are departures: every verb (a meeting, a cable, a forgery, a bank drawing) has a duration and competes for the slack before the 14:05, so travel, deception, items, economy and politics are one game before any of them is deep. The hunt reads the same Bradshaw, the diary is the scheduler's face, and the engine is the fifth directive made playable: one priority queue, seed plus input log, exact replay. Its hook is the pool's most honest: Zeigarnik tension from a booked departure, the near-miss of a connection made by eleven minutes, slack as a mastery curve, and sessions that end aboard a night train, the natural stopping point players refuse. Routes as owned, dated knowledge give thirty years of progression that lives in the player's head. Everything else attaches to this skeleton.

P10.statement: C04 is the concept every other candidate presupposes: a legend is the unit of account. Money (C08) is a ledger per name; traces (C17) are records under a name; hunters (C05, C03) keep a dossier per name and advance only by linking two; standing, households, debts and nationality attach to names, not to the player. That is the touchstone career made mechanical, and it realises all five directives at once: lives run in real cities under real registration regimes (Britain invents, Germany audits), travel is the circuit that keeps lives provably incompatible, deception is what each name asserts, the hunt is linkage, and the world clock (1914 internment, 1915 photographs) raises the price of every name you kept. Its hook is honest: endowment over lives you built, and granular failure, lose a name, not the game. Nine panelists proposed it independently.
